full_judgment:
2. The short facts leading to this petition are that one Gouranga Chandra Dey who is respondent No. 1 earlier instituted Title Suit No. 68 of 1990 in the third Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for specific performance of contract against the predecessor of the petitioner. That suit was earlier dismissed, against which respondent No. I preferred Title Appeal No. 57 of 111 1977 before the lower appellate Court. The appellate Court set aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court and sent back the case on remand for fresh trial - Against that order of remand the present petitioner preferred Second Appeal No. 966 of 1978 before the High Court Division which was dismissed. Then the original .suit was taken up and re-numbered as Title Suit No. 68 of '1990 which was decreed ex parte in favour of respondent No. 1 who ultimately put the decree, into execution in Execution Case No. 18 of '1994 and got the sale deed which was registered. Thereafter the present petitioner filed Title Suit No. 244 of 1994 for a declaration that the ex parte decree passed in Title Suit. No. 68 of 1990 was illegal and void. In this suit an application was filed for rejection of the plaint under Order 7 Rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure by respondent. No 1. After hearing the parties the trial Court rejected the plaint as prayed for and against that order of rejection of the plaint, First Appeal Tender No. 498 of 1998 has been filed by the Petitioner which is pending before the High Court Division. After filing of this First Appeal Tender the petitioner filed an application for slaying all further proceedings of Execution Case No. 18 of 1994 now pending before the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka and then the present Rule was issued and an ad interim order of stay was granted. Thereafter on hearing the learned Advocates of both sides the Division Bench of the High Court Division by judgment dated 17.5.1999 discharged the Rule. 

 3. Mr. Md. Fazlul Karim learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that though a sale deed was obtained and registered by respondent No. 1 in Execution Case No. 18 of 1994 this petitioner is still in possession grid as the suit he filed is for a declaration that the parte decree passed in Title Suit No. 68 of 19..)0 was illegal and void in all fairness pending proposal of First Anneal Tender No. 498 of 1998 of the High ct Division:1- further proceedings of the aforesaid execution case be stayed. 

 4. Admitted position is that In pursuance to the decree passed in Title Suit No. 68 of 1990 which was a suit for specific performance of contract, the plaintiff got the kabala executed and registered through Court and it appears that possession was also obtained in most of the suit land excepting of course a very small fraction of the land which is in possession of some unauthorised persons. The High Court Division found that since the decree has already been executed in Execution Case No. 18 of 1994 and the kabala has been registered on 20.10.1994 there is nothing to stay all further proceedings of the aforesaid execution case. The petitioner filed Title Suit No. 244 of 1994 for a declaration that the ex parte decree passed in Title Suit No. 68 of 1990 was illegal and void which has nothing to do with the aforesaid execution proceeding and when the decree obtained by respondent No. I has already been executed, we are of the view that the High Court Division has not committed any wrong or illegality in refusing to stay further proceedings of aforesaid Execution Case No. 18 of 1994. Mr. Karim failed to make out any case for our interference in the matter. There is therefore no merit in this petition.
